detail.readme:
InfiniDysk

Your media library, streamed from Usenet.

InfiniDysk is a Usenet-backed virtual filesystem. Sonarr, Radarr and other Arr apps add it as a SABnzbd download client. It never downloads the release: your media server reads the files over a native FUSE mount or WebDAV, and InfiniDysk streams them from your Usenet providers on demand. This is InfiniDysk **2.0**, rewritten in Rust and now in **beta**. Docs: [infinidysk.com](https://www.infinidysk.com/). Chat: [Discord](https://discord.gg/DAya7W6QMa). Bugs and ideas: [issues](https://github.com/infinidysk/infinidysk/issues). > [!WARNING] > **Moving from 1.x to 2.x is a breaking change.** It needs manual steps: copy your config, run the import, and replace the rclone sidecar with the built-in mount. Changing the image name alone is not an upgrade. Some 1.x features are not in 2.x yet. > > [Pick a version](https://www.infinidysk.com/) first. To move, follow [Upgrade from 1.x](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/upgrade/), and check [what is not in 2.x yet](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/whats-new/#feature-comparison). ## Looking for 1.x? 1.x (the C# version) lives on the [`v1`](https://github.com/infinidysk/infinidysk/tree/v1) branch and keeps the `ghcr.io/infinidysk/infinidysk` image. It gets bug fixes only. Its docs are at [infinidysk.com/v1](https://www.infinidysk.com/v1/). If your fork tracks 1.x, move it to `v1`: ```sh git fetch upstream git push origin upstream/v1:refs/heads/v1 ``` Then set your fork's default branch to `v1` and sync that branch from now on. A fork with its own commits merges `upstream/v1` instead of `upstream/main`; it is the same history, so there are no new conflicts. ## Quick start A new install. Coming from 1.x? Follow [Upgrade from 1.x](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/upgrade/) instead, so your library and history carry over. ```yaml services: infinidysk: image: ghcr.io/infinidysk/infinidysk-next:edge container_name: infinidysk restart: unless-stopped environment: PUID: 1000 PGID: 1000 TZ: Etc/UTC # your time zone, e.g. Europe/Oslo; the maintenance window follows it ports: - "3000:3000" volumes: - ./config:/config - /mnt:/mnt:rshared - /sys/devices/virtual/bdi:/sys/devices/virtual/bdi:rw devices: - /dev/fuse:/dev/fuse cap_add: - SYS_ADMIN security_opt: - apparmor:unconfined ``` Open `http://:3000`, create the admin account, then add your providers. Do this before exposing the port to an untrusted network: until an admin exists, anyone who reaches the page can create one. The UI, the SABnzbd API and WebDAV share port 3000. The library is mounted at `/mnt/infinidysk`. The image is `ghcr.io/infinidysk/infinidysk-next` for Linux x64 and arm64; `edge` is the newest 2.x release, every release also has its own `v2.x.y` tag, and there is no `latest` tag until 2.0 ships. Next steps in the docs: [Run with Docker](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/install/docker/), [Providers](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/install/providers/), [Connect your Arr apps](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/install/connect-arr/), [Settings](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/reference/settings/). ## Reporting problems See [Reporting a bug](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/help/reporting/): the image tag, a support pack from the System page, and for playback problems a read trace. Never post provider passwords or API keys. Release names are not needed; describe the file instead (for example "stored RAR5 episode"). ## Development 1.x bug fixes go to the `v1` branch; everything else targets `main`. Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the project rules and [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) before changing the UI. Requires [rustup](https://rustup.rs); the toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`. ```sh cargo fmt --all --check cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings cargo test --workspace --locked ``` ## License MIT
